name: Peninsula and the Old Town
tagline: The headland where Tomis stood, with the casino on the point
description: The historic peninsula holding the Roman mosaic building, the Great Mahmudiye Mosque, the Orthodox cathedral and the derelict Art Nouveau casino on the seafront. It is the most interesting part of Constanta and the most neglected, with restoration proceeding slowly through a quarter full of empty buildings.
bestFor: Stays that want the Roman and Ottoman layers rather than the resort
pros: Roman mosaics, the mosque and the casino within a short walk
Sea on three sides and a genuine old-town character
Low rents for a central position
cons: Visibly run down with many empty buildings
Quiet and poorly lit at night

name: City Centre and Tomis Boulevard
tagline: The commercial core, where the city actually works
description: The modern centre along Bulevardul Tomis, with the shops, the offices, the market, the university and the transport connections. It is unremarkable to look at and by far the most practical place to base yourself, with the best rental supply and everything reachable on foot or a short bus.
bestFor: Anyone who wants services, the market and buses within a short walk
pros: All shops, banks and services close by
The best rental supply in the city
Buses to Mamaia and the beaches
cons: Traffic and noise on the boulevard

name: Mamaia
tagline: The resort strip on the sand spit, Romania's summer capital
description: A narrow strip of land between the sea and Lake Siutghiol, built end to end with hotels, clubs and apartment towers, and the centre of Romanian summer nightlife from June to September. Out of season it empties almost completely, which makes winter rents here unexpectedly cheap.
bestFor: Summer stays that want the beach and the clubs, or winter stays that want them empty
pros: Beach on one side, lake and watersports on the other
cons: Expensive and extremely loud in July and August
Fifteen to twenty minutes into the city

name: Faleza Nord
tagline: The clifftop north of the centre, sea views and quiet
description: The residential district on the cliff between the city and Mamaia, with apartment blocks looking straight out over the Black Sea, a promenade along the edge and beaches below. It is quieter than either the centre or the resort and sits within walking distance of both.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a sea view without resort pricing or city noise
pros: Sea views and a clifftop promenade
Walking distance to both the centre and Mamaia
cons: Exposed to the wind off the sea

name: Tomis Nord and the Northern Estates
tagline: The residential blocks inland, cheapest rents in the city
description: The large socialist-era housing districts north and west of the centre, with supermarkets, schools, markets and frequent buses. Nothing here is attractive, the flats are larger than in the centre and the rents are the lowest in Constanta, which for a long stay is the calculation.
bestFor: Long stays where the rent is the deciding factor
pros: The lowest rents in the city
Larger flats and full everyday shopping
Frequent buses to the centre and the beaches
cons: Nothing to walk to in the evening
